title: Mixtures of released infrared color templates do not weaken the dust bound for 78 young CPV hosts
abstract: We test whether positive mixtures of ten released infrared color templates can hide more dust energy than one temperature. We use the Ks/W1, W2/W1 and W3/W1 signal and joint bootstrap covariance for 78 young complex periodic variable hosts and 417 non-hosts. A convex optimization with matching dual certificates finds that the largest total weight uses only the hottest allowed template in all 27 tested settings. For the grid from 700 to 2,000 K, the effective absorbed-fraction upper bound in a nominal 95% joint Gaussian region is 0.00734. It is 0.01271 when standard errors grow by 50%, and 0.01744 when they double. The source persistent summed-depth requirement is 0.01558. Thus temperature mixing does not weaken this finite-template test, but enlarged errors can permit the required energy. These are bounds for a linear cone of released aggregate color templates. They are not an exact fit to multi-temperature dust spectra, nor a bound for arbitrary continuous temperatures or historical material duty. We include original code, aggregate results, input hashes and numerical certificates.

display.caption: Joint-region bounds over positive mixtures of released temperature templates. Temperature mixing does not increase the bound; larger temperature ceilings and errors do.
